summary.intent: Fix Python manifest range rewriting in the callisto-manifests crate so Poetry caret and tilde specs (and one-minor windows) round-trip correctly, then ship it as a PR with tests, a spec criterion and a changeset.
summary.outcome: Poetry caret/tilde rewriting was implemented in python.rs with tests asserting the written form, verified against a real Poetry and PEP 621 fixture using the rebuilt binary. Spec criterion VER-CAS-09 and a changeset were added, CI was run, and the Python range PR was committed and opened.

repo: Python range handling lives in crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs, with tests in python/tests.rs; Poetry spec normalization is handled separately from PEP 621 ranges.
Round-trip results from the range code are not the final string: the cascade converts them into the written spec string, so the rendered form can differ from what round_trip returns.
Behavior specs live in docs/specs/versioning.json; cascade rewrite behavior is tracked as VER-CAS-* criteria (VER-CAS-09 added for Python range rewriting).
Changes in this repo are expected to ship with a changeset and a passing CI run before the PR is opened.
Work was done in a dedicated git worktree for the Python change.

code.finding: Contains the compound range rewrite, Poetry spec normalization (read and write) and parse_version_core; caret/tilde handling and one-minor windows were changed here. Exact line numbers were not shown in the transcript.
Existing round_trip tests were extended and then changed to assert the written (rendered) form of Poetry specs rather than only the round-trip result.
Holds the VER-CAS criteria list; the new VER-CAS-09 criterion for Python range rewriting was appended after the last existing one.

workflow: Verify fixes against the real built binary with a fixture (a scratchpad validate_py.sh script covering Poetry and PEP 621), not only unit tests.
Inspect the actual rendered output before writing assertions, so tests pin the user-visible written form.
Rebuild the binary after changes before rerunning fixtures to avoid testing a stale build.
Run formatting and re-read the tests afterward, since formatting can change the code being edited.

friction: The round-trip result did not match the written string, so tests had to be rewritten after tracing the cascade code path to see how the spec string is produced.
Several rounds of reading code were needed to find where the written Python spec string is generated and where Python range rewriting is specified.
Formatting changed the Poetry tests, requiring a re-read before the next edit.
